static_traits.name: Wang Lina
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, parents living in another state
static_traits.social_status: The relationship with fishing-loving friends is getting tense, often feeling inferior from comparing with them; having a few friends to confide in, but they do not share the fishing passion and cannot understand her inadequacy
static_traits.medical_history: without significant physical illness; not yet received psychotherapy before; similar psychological problems had not appeared in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good cooperativeness; negative emotional tone; often using absolute language (e.g. 'never' 'complete failure'); tending to compare with others

basic_info.main_problem: I keep feeling I will never become good at fishing, especially after multiple outings with no catch, this feeling is more pronounced.
basic_info.core_demands: The ongoing inadequacy and Self-doubt around fishing have begun affecting my overall confidence and enjoyment of leisure activities, so I seek counseling.
growth_experiences: On a fishing trip with Father years ago, catching nothing at all started strong inadequacy; stress was moderate then, feeling the need to perform as excellently as Father in fishing; since then every catch-less outing triggers low self-esteem and Sense of frustration, gradually turning the leisure experience into a source of stress.

core_beliefs: I will never become an excellent angler

special_situations.event: On the fishing trip with Father, not catching any fish
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot perform as excellently as Father in fishing, it shows I am a failure, not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Through reading fishing guides, watching teaching videos, and increasing practice, proves oneself and improves technique
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never be as good as Father, I disappointed him

special_situations.event: Each solo fishing trip often with no catch
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I catch no fish again this time, it proves I have never been good and will never improve
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling research on methods, frequently trying different techniques, but continuously using catch as the sole success criterion
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never become a good angler in this lifetime

special_situations.event: Fishing with friends or seeing friends get a better catch
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not catch as many or as well as friends, it shows I have no value, I am terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Talking less with friends about fishing, constantly comparing others' performance in mind for self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them, I am terrible

special_situations.event: When occasionally catching a small fish, compares with others' catches
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only reaching high standards or significant achievements like others counts as success, otherwise it does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating her small progress, focusing on others' better performance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This does not count as success, this is meaningless

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized, seen, and affirmed before significant others (especially father)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and seeming inferior after comparison, thus being judged and belittled
defense_goal: Suppressing the craving for recognition through self-reproach and constant comparison to avoid further disappointment; keeping distance in fishing-related relationships to reduce the risk of being judged

object_relations.self_representation: A failure who is not good enough and needs to prove herself
object_relations.object_representation: A judge with high standards who easily compares (represented by the father)

object_relations.self_representation: A participant who is always behind and inferior in front of peers
object_relations.object_representation: More accomplished competitors beyond one's reach (fishing friends)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites me to acknowledge small progress or effort, or asks whether there were moments of pride
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client subconsciously believes 'these do not count', the positive will be negated (transference: she may be judged at any time)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Validating her feelings in a gentle Empathic tone, using concrete Questioning (e.g. having her describe one specific attempt and process), avoiding direct refutation, gradually Guiding her to acknowledge small progress.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests transferring successful work experience to the fishing domain
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes 'fishing is a completely different field', therefore unchangeable (treating the possibility of change as ineffective)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Keeping a neutral, open tone, using open-ended questions to have her give examples of similarities and differences, encouraging her to identify transferable micro-skills, avoiding judgmental language.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the topic involves comparisons with the father or friends and experiences of failure
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning external pressure and judgment against the self, believing all problems are her own, she is not good enough
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: With a steady, low-intensity Empathic tone, helping her distinguish external standards from self-worth, using reflective Listening and gentle reframing, encouraging her to identify self-critical language and switch to neutral descriptions.

manifestations: Having a few friends to confide in, but they do not understand her fishing passion and inadequacy
Tense relationships with fishing-loving friends, interactions becoming difficult
outcomes: Declining leisure experience quality and Increased stress

manifestations: Fishing once brought calm and closeness-to-nature experiences, but now overshadowed by failure and Self-doubt
outcomes: Leisure activities no longer relaxing and nourishing, turned into a source of stress
Finds it hard to focus on process value, only focuses on the result (whether there is a catch)

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats the father's high standards and excellent performance as standards she must achieve
Judges himself by the belief that 'only catching a fish counts as success'

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When invited to attend to the pleasure of the process (nature, calm), finds it hard to engage and quickly shifts to outcomes and failure
Jokes about or downplays small progress and feedback, hard to acknowledge directly

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently evaluates fishing performance through self-criticism
Overly concerned about others' standards and comparison with friends on fishing topics

positive_force: Persistently invests in learning and trying (reading guides, watching videos)
Having achievement and Self-efficacy in the Work domain
Willing to try shifting attention to the process, accepting counseling and practice
Has experienced the calm of fishing and the value of closeness to nature
negative_force: Excessively compares others' performance; external standards dominate self-worth
Black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization (one failure means concluding she is no good)
Future-predicting despair ('I will never become a good angler in this lifetime')
Personalization tendency (attributing no catch to her own incompetence)

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Self-denial and Anxiety when fishing fails or catches are few (words like 'I can never become a good angler')
antecedent: Fishing with Father or friends with no catch
Solo outings frequently with no catch
Comparing after seeing others' better catches
target_behavior.core_reason: Influenced by Father's high standards and comparison pressure, tying self-worth to fishing results, and maintaining Self-deprecation and Anxiety driven by cognitive distortions (black-and-white, overgeneralization, negating the positive, predicting the future)
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the Anxiety of failure and being judged, seeking control or finding 'reasons' for poor results through Self-denial; while trying to gain external recognition through harder Learning and attempts
target_behavior.consequence: Leisure activities turned into a source of stress, overall Decreased confidence; tense relationships with fishing friends, unable to enjoy the process and relax
